stable_agency_screen.criteria: At least 50 CONUS positive-acreage source records and >=90% nonmissing containment dates in EACH of all 24 early/recent target years; absent years fail.
stable_agency_screen.conclusion: No reporting agency satisfies the specified annual high-coverage screen.
stable_agency_screen.threshold_caveat: These screening thresholds are diagnostic choices, not a guarantee of reporting stability or a causal identification rule; values just below 90% should not be interpreted as a qualitative discontinuity.

definitions.coverage_denominators: containment_date_fraction_source uses all source records; eligible fractions use CONUS coordinates and positive acreage; clock-complete fraction uses the usable containment cohort. Undefined zero-denominator fractions are null.
definitions.calendar_outcome: Normalized containment date minus normalized discovery date; source timestamps remain untouched. Containment is not fire-out.
definitions.FS_only: Records whose NWCG reporting agency is FS; this is not all fires on Forest Service land and does not hold reporting units, geography, weather, policy, or fire mix fixed.
definitions.clock_complete: Both source HHMM clocks are valid, including 2400 as end-of-day midnight, and the resulting interval remains within 0–365 days. Source clocks have unspecified timezones.
definitions.raw_quantiles: Unweighted empirical calendar-day quantiles using linear interpolation; wall-clock sensitivity quantiles use only clock-complete records.
definitions.standardization: Within each broad size bin and scope, retain finer-acreage/agency strata with at least the configured count in each period. Reweight recent records to early-period common-support stratum proportions; early records have unit weights. Overall stratifies by finer acreage and agency; FS-only by finer acreage.
definitions.standardized_quantiles: Inverse weighted empirical CDF (step quantiles), not interpolation. Interpret standardized and raw quantile differences with this small estimator distinction in mind.

caveats: All results are observed descriptive comparisons or composition-standardized descriptive sensitivities, not causal estimates of suppression effectiveness.
Aggregate Forest Service containment coverage masks a major recent decline; FS-only is another biased descriptive sensitivity, not a clean or stable reporting control.
Missing containment outcomes need not resemble reported outcomes; neither complete-case analysis nor composition weighting identifies their unobserved durations.
Early and recent periods span different numbers of years. Raw record counts are support sizes, not comparable annual incidence rates.
Final acreage is a fire outcome, not a pre-incident severity measure; broad and finer size matching cannot isolate suppression capability.

Finer-acreage/agency standardization addresses only those observed mixture differences on shared support; weather, geography, resource use, management policy, and reporting changes remain uncontrolled.
Subday clock availability changes by year and agency. The primary comparison consistently uses calendar days; clocks-only sensitivities select a different population.
Same-calendar-day containment is not instantaneous containment; calendar quantiles cannot resolve within-day improvements or delays.
These audit summaries have no causal confidence intervals; they describe the available records and their measured composition.
Changing the early/recent window endpoints changes the observed tail-duration contrast; neither a short nor broad window identifies a causal suppression effect.

checks: exact reconstructed eligibility versus cohort IDs
calendar outcomes equal normalized source date subtraction
clock flags and wall-clock outcomes match source clocks
coverage tables recover source and cohort totals
weighted quantiles agree with replicated empirical quantiles
